formulas.formula: Know what you have, what's selling, and what to make next.
1. Categories: list the kinds of things you sell (Candles, Soaps, Stickers...).
2. Products: one row per item with its SKU (a short code), cost to make or buy, sale price, how many you have now, and the reorder point.
3. Sales: log every sale with the date, SKU and quantity. Leave Price Each blank to use the list price.
4. Stock In: log restocks and batches you make. Use a minus number for damaged, lost or used items.
5. Products now shows what's on hand, stock value and status. Reorder List shows what to make or buy next.
6. Monthly Summary, Best Sellers and Dashboard update on their own.
Any short code works (CN-08-LAV, 1001). Type it the same way on Sales and Stock In; capitals don't matter.
What you had on the day you started tracking. Don't change it later; log changes on Stock In.
Revenue minus cost of goods, fees and shipping you paid. Cost of goods uses each product's Unit Cost.
Set the year on Products. Monthly numbers and best sellers follow it; stock on hand counts everything.
Clear the white cells on Sales and Stock In (from row 6 down) and the sample products.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: in stock, or making money.
Yellow: at or under the reorder point.
Red: out of stock, a SKU that isn't on Products, or something to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Happy selling.

One row per item. Type the white columns; On Hand and everything after it calculate from Sales and Stock In.
One row per item sold. Leave Price Each blank to use the product's sale price. Fees = what the platform kept; Shipping = what you paid to ship.
Restocks and batches you make (plus numbers). Damaged, lost or used items (minus numbers). Unit Cost is optional; it adds up your restock spending.
Everything at or under its reorder point, plus anything sold out. Order Qty uses Reorder Qty from Products (or tops you back up to the reorder point).
Every month of the year on the Products tab. Profit = revenue minus cost of goods, fees and shipping.
